At 9.20 on Wednesday morning, 900 children were halfway through the early shift at Tribhuvan Trishuli secondary school, a three-storey complex in the Trishuli valley of north-central Nepal.⁠ ⁠ Another 700 were on their way on foot and by bus, when the principal, Rajendra Dadabi, received a panicked call from a friend in Betrawati, five miles upstream. “He said the village was gone: taken by the river,” said Dadabi. “He told me to run.”⁠ ⁠ The 47-year-old English teacher took a moment to consider the threat. He remembered that the school buses, each carrying 80 children, were en route.⁠ ⁠ “I got through to all the drivers but one and told them to turn back. Then I saw the bus I hadn’t been able to contact coming across the bridge. By now, the water was in the school grounds — it was so fast — so I told him to turn around. It got to the other side just as the bridge collapsed.”⁠ ⁠ Dadabi’s quick thinking saved the lives of 1,643 children and all but one member of the teaching staff. #nepal #nepalfloods #floods

More than 1,300 people are missing in Nepal and Tibet, including 47 Americans, after a glacial collapse caused catastrophic floods, with video showing mud sweeping through entire communities. Drone footage in Nepal showed roads destroyed and buildings buried by thundering water the color of wet cement. Nepalese authorities ramped up operations in the worst-affected districts of Nuwakot and Rasuwa. The disaster in Nepal and Tibet is not a one-off. The Lhende Khola river system has now flooded twice in just 14 months and the increasingly unstable Himalayan ice system threatens communities, infrastructure and water supplies across one of the world’s most densely populated regions. The region saw similar flash floods in August last year, when a glacial lake in Tibet overflowed because of high temperatures. Nine people were killed, and critical infrastructure, including a bridge connecting Nepal and China, was damaged.

My heart has been so heavy watching what is happening across Nepal 💔🇳🇵 Nepal is such a special place to me, It’s where I met my husband, where my family live and where I spend most of my days. Some of the most important memories of my life were made here. Ive seen so much of its beauty, but I’ve also come to understand how much strength and resilience its people carry… Seeing communities affected by these floods is incredibly difficult for me. People whose homes, businesses, farms and livelihoods have been taken away in a matter of hours. There are people worrying about their loved ones, people who have been forced to leave everything behind, and people simply trying to get through another day safely. My thoughts are with everyone affected, especially those who have lost loved ones or everything they had. I’m also thinking of the people working tirelessly to help, rescue and support those in need. I know I can’t change what has happened, but I can use my voice to remind people that Nepal needs support, attention and compassion right now… Praying for the safety of everyone across the country, for the families waiting for their loved ones, and for the strength to rebuild when the water finally goes down. While the powerful floodwaters caused widespread destruction nearby, the house remarkably managed to survive, leaving viewers stunned by the sight. Viewers were amazed by the incredible scene, with many calling it a miracle that the house remained standing while the surrounding area was heavily affected. Others were left wondering how the structure managed to withstand such powerful flooding. Heavy floods caused devastation across the area, but one house remarkably survived, turning the scene into a powerful reminder of how unpredictable nature can be. #ViralVideo #NepalFloods #Miracle #Nepal #MiraculousMoment

What is happening in Nepal is a devastating reminder that the climate crisis does not respect borders. 💔🌎 A catastrophic glacier collapse has triggered deadly flooding across the Himalayas, leaving hundreds dead and more than a thousand people missing. Scientists say a warming climate is making glaciers less stable and increasing the risks of these kinds of cascading disasters. Sadly, Nepal has one of the lowest per-capita carbon footprints in the world, yet it is among the countries most vulnerable to the impacts of climate change. The people who contribute the least to the problem are often the ones paying the highest price. This is why climate action cannot simply be about individual choices. It has to be about changing systems, holding the biggest emitters accountable, and making sure vulnerable communities are protected. Climate change may feel far away .. until it isn’t. It affects all of us. But it does not affect all of us equally. Our hearts are with the people of Nepal and everyone affected by this unimaginable tragedy. 🇳🇵💔 #Nepal #ClimateChange #ClimateJustice #fy #ClimateAction footage by onlookers via Damall
